correctness.rationale: For Bernoulli data, log wealth at time \(s\) is affine in the integer success count \(K_s\), so rejection is exactly \(K_s\ge\lceil q_s(\beta)\rceil\). The effective first-passage boundary vector therefore changes only when some \(q_s\) crosses an integer. Differentiation gives \(q'_s(\beta)=[s(\beta\kappa'(\beta)-\kappa(\beta))-\log(1/\alpha)]/(\beta^2\Delta)\), while \(\beta\kappa'(\beta)-\kappa(\beta)\) is strictly increasing because \(\kappa''>0\). Hence each \(q_s\) has at most one minimum and each relevant integer level at most two roots, proving finitely many cells. The package verifier exhaustively enumerates the \(t=30\) cells and exact rational survival probabilities, certifying the displayed plateau and comparison point.
